source_ref: Ding X, Zhao Z, Wang J, Chen C, Ding S, Gao J, Deng J, Liu D (2025) Relationships between different components of intolerance of uncertainty and symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder: a network analysis, PeerJ 13:e19791, doi:10.7717/peerj.19791 (PMC12318506, CC BY 4.0): Methods 'Measures' (anchors) and Table 1 (item wording for IU1-IU8, IU10-IU12 with M(SD)), fetched as Europe PMC fullTextXML (sha256 c8040d67...13ea); supplements via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip: peerj-13-19791-s001.tsv (headerless data, sha256 d49a749d...4899) and peerj-13-19791-s002.docx (Table S1, 18x12 OCD x IU correlation matrix, sha256 2608f605...fa38). IU9 wording from PhenX Toolkit protocol PX650701 'Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale (IUS)', https://www.phenxtoolkit.org/protocols/view/650701 (fetched 2026-09-27; page prints its retrieval date so no stable hash). Processing script data/ding_2025_iu_ocd.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/ding_2025_iu/.
note: CODE DERIVATION: positional -- data/ding_2025_iu_ocd.py reads the headerless .tsv and names columns 2..13 IU1..IU12 by position, following the paper's own node labels. No header exists to diff, so the mapping was verified statistically (verify_ding_2025_iu.R): Spearman correlations of live IU1..IU12 with live OCD1..OCD18 (N=1551) reproduce all 216 cells of Supplementary Table S1 to max |diff| 0.0005 (S1 printed to 3 dp); each IU column's RMSE to its own published column is 0.0003 vs >=0.0159 to any other column, so every item including IU9 is pinned. Table 1 means also match on the full N=1551 (largest deviation 0.005 over the 11 printed items). TEXT: 11 of 12 items verbatim from the paper's Table 1 (curly apostrophes kept, no trailing periods, as printed). IU9 is NOT printed anywhere in the paper or supplements (the item was dropped from the network as redundant with IU10); its wording is inferred BY ELIMINATION: Table 1's 11 items are exactly 11 of the 12 IUS-12 items (Carleton, Norton & Asmundson 2007), and the one absent is 'When it's time to act, uncertainty paralyses me', transcribed from the PhenX IUS page (item 12 of the IUS-27 there) with its trailing period dropped to match the paper's style. Consistent with the paper's report that IU9 and IU10 ('When I am uncertain I can't function very well') are near-redundant, and with live IU9's S1 fingerprint being closest to IU10. This assumes the C-IUS-12 (Zhang et al. 2017) keeps Carleton's 12 items, which the paper's naming implies but which was not checked against Zhang 2017. LANGUAGE: administered in Chinese (C-IUS-12). Checked the deposit .tsv (headerless, numbers only) and s002.docx (labels IU1..IU12 only; zero CJK item text) -- no Chinese wording recoverable, so English ships in the base fields with language=Chinese (fallback). translation_source=mixed: IU1-8, IU10-12 and the two anchors are the study's own English (study_supplied); IU9 is the PhenX-distributed instrument English (official_instrument_english). OPTIONS: the paper labels only the endpoints, 1 = 'Not at all characteristic of me' and 5 = 'Entirely characteristic of me'; resp 2-4 rows ship with option_text blank rather than importing canonical middle anchors the study never states. Instructions left blank: the study prints none, and PhenX's IUS-27 instructions are a different form. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv row 'Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale (IUS, 27 items)' verdict ship_with_note applied (short form inherits the parent row, as the reaudit triage for this table recorded). Quoted from PhenX: 'This protocol is freely available; permission not required for use.' That is a distributor statement, not an originator grant; no originator terms for the IUS or IUS-12 were located, so nothing reserves a right. Wording for 11 items came from a CC BY 4.0 article. Sample note: Table 1/S1 were computed on all 1551 deposit rows although the Methods report a final sample of 1529 after excluding under-18s; the live table matches the 1551.
public_note: Administered in Chinese (C-IUS-12); the English shown is the study's own for 11 items, while IU9's wording is not printed by the study and is the standard IUS-12 item 'When it's time to act, uncertainty paralyses me', inferred by elimination.
